record.title: Preprint derives sharp force-space density thresholds for forced Navier–Stokes breakdown
record.summary: Cao, Chi, and Nie report sharp thresholds for how close smooth forcing can be, in weak Sobolev norms, while producing classical breakdown by a prescribed time. For fixed positive viscosity and zero initial velocity, their preprint claims density exactly below s=1/2 in relative L1_t H^s_x on both T3 and R3; on R3 it gives the corresponding L2_t H^s_x threshold s<-1/2. The construction glues in a compact forced blowup block attributed to OpenAI while changing the external force. These are preprint claims not independently reproduced here, and they do not address the unforced Millennium problem or independently verify the building block.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Cao, Chi, and Nie posted v1 of this preprint on 2026-09-09; the inspected v4 manuscript is dated 2026-09-22 and presents a force-space density theorem for classical breakdown in three-dimensional Navier–Stokes equations.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors claim that for fixed positive viscosity and zero initial velocity, smooth external forces producing classical breakdown by T are dense in the relative L1_t H^s_x topology exactly for s<1/2 on both the three-torus and R3. On R3 they also claim the corresponding L2_t H^s_x threshold is exactly s<-1/2. The torus theorem additionally gives density below s=1/2 for each fixed admissible smooth initial velocity.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The construction inserts a rescaled compact forced blowup solution into a region where a smooth cutoff of a local vector potential makes the surrounding velocity vanish; it adjusts the external force and preserves the initial velocity and earlier history.

claims.label: INFERRED
claims.text: The result concerns force-dependent classical breakdown and weak force-space topologies; it does not resolve the unforced Navier–Stokes regularity problem or independently validate the compact blowup solution used as its building block.

evidence_gaps.description: The density arguments and sharpness claims remain author-reported in a preprint; the research desk has not obtained independent PDE review or reproduced the analysis.

The paper relies on the compact forced blowup solution attributed to OpenAI. The linked Lean repository and author-controlled CI are not an independent construction or semantic audit of that building block.

brief.importance_rationale: If correct, sharp force-space density thresholds would materially inform mathematical understanding of instability under weakly measured forcing and guide which force norms can control classical breakdown. The result remains a preprint, changes the external force, and depends on an attributed compact blowup block, so its bounded theoretical consequence does not warrant a higher score.
limitations: All theorem statements and proofs are author claims in an arXiv preprint; the research desk did not independently verify the analysis.
The construction changes the external force and relies on a compact forced blowup solution attributed to OpenAI; it is not an independent proof of that building block.
The results concern force-dependent breakdown and specified Lq_t H^s_x topologies, not unforced Navier–Stokes regularity or resolution of the Clay Millennium problem.
The linked Lean formalization and its paper-to-code correspondence were not built or audited during this review.

For fixed positive viscosity and zero initial velocity, their preprint claims density exactly below s=1/2 in relative L1_t H^s_x on both T3 and R3; on R3 it gives the corresponding L2_t H^s_x threshold s<-1/2. technical.claimed_result: For fixed positive viscosity and zero initial velocity, the paper claims density of smooth forces producing classical breakdown by T exactly for s<1/2 in relative L1_t H^s_x on T3 and R3. On R3, the L2_t H^s_x threshold is s<-1/2. For each fixed admissible smooth initial velocity on T3, the density result holds below s=1/2.
technical.demonstrated_result: the research desk directly inspected the v4 arXiv manuscript and verified that it states these theorems and describes the construction. the research desk did not verify the proofs, run a reproduction, or independently establish the underlying compact blowup solution.
technical.mechanism: A divergence-free cutoff applied to a local vector potential makes a given smooth velocity vanish near a small region; a rescaled compact forced blowup solution is inserted there. The surrounding and inserted velocities have no mixed nonlinear interaction, while a smooth correction is absorbed into a changed external force.
technical.regime: Three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes with fixed positive viscosity and smooth external force, on T3 or R3, for classical breakdown by prescribed time T. The sharp iff thresholds are stated for zero initial velocity; the torus density-below-threshold result also covers fixed admissible smooth initial velocities.
technical.strongest_baseline: No empirical baseline applies. The paper contrasts its classical-breakdown result with earlier force-density results for nonunique Leray–Hopf solutions and derives the stated threshold from its own proof and critical-regularity estimates.

brief.title: Preprint derives sharp force-space density thresholds for forced Navier–Stokes breakdown
brief.why_it_matters: If correct, the sharp thresholds characterize when smooth forcing can be made arbitrarily small in specified weak norms while still causing classical breakdown, clarifying the sensitivity of forced Navier–Stokes dynamics. The result is mathematically significant but conditional: the construction changes the force and imports a separate compact blowup solution, and neither proof has been independently checked by the research desk.
